land.text: the modern state formed in 1895 when Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined the Seri Menanti Confederation

successors.note: 'The domains of Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined this confederation in 1895', and the state 'joined the Federated Malay States the same year' (Negeri Sembilan page); the Treaty of Federation 1895 'formally went into effect on 1 July 1896' (Federated Malay States page). Negeri Sembilan continues as a state of the FMS, then of Malaya (1948).

capitals.name: Seri Menanti (Kuala Pilah District)
capitals.note: The page calls Seri Menanti the royal capital in Kuala Pilah District and gives the title Yamtuan Seri Menanti in 1773, but no date for the seat; coordinates approximate. Its palace was destroyed in the 1875 fighting at Bukit Putus (page, undated sentence).

correction.text: the confederation of 1773 as Cliopatria draws it from 1775

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives the nine-chiefdom confederation under a Yamtuan Seri Menanti in 1773, two years before Cliopatria's first shape. The 1775 outline is carried back.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, valid 1773-1873; Naning and Sungai Ujong leave by ledger events 1832 and 1874

keyframe_review.note: 5,900 km2 against the infobox 6,686 km2 for the modern state (ratio 0.88). The page lists nine original chiefdoms of 1773 (Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Rembau, Johol, Jelai, Ulu Pahang, Naning, Segamat, Klang); Cliopatria's outline holds no Selangor cell and stops at lon 102.67, so it omits at least Klang and Segamat, which the page says were annexed 'in the 19th century' without years. The outline stands for the surviving luaks. Years: it holds to 1873 (Cliopatria changes it in 1873, a year before the page's 1874 British intervention in Sungai Ujong); Naning leaves in 1832 (ledger).

3,655 km2: the 1775 shape without four H3 cells at and south-east of Seremban (Sungai Ujong and its neighbourhood). 'In 1874, the British intervened militarily in a leadership tussle in Sungai Ujong' and the domain went under a British Resident; the shape applies from 1874, not 1873, and still holds Jelebu until 1883 (ledger).

3,626 km2: same cells as 1873, the area differs by under one percent and no page dates a change in 1877. Jelebu is inside this outline until 1890 although the page puts a British Resident there in 1883 ('Jelebu followed in 1883'); the ledger's 1883 loss takes effect inside this keyframe.

2,159 km2, 0.32 of the infobox 6,686 km2, beyond a factor of two: the shape is the Seri Menanti Confederation of 1889 ('the Seri Menanti domain' joined with Tampin and Rembau), without Sungai Ujong and Jelebu, which only 'joined this confederation in 1895'. The infobox is the modern state after that union, so the shape is right for 1890-1894 and the infobox is the wrong yardstick; the ledger's 1895 gains close the gap.

correction.text: the modern state, formed in 1895 from the Seri Menanti Confederation, Sungai Ujong and Jelebu

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The domains of Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined this confederation in 1895', forming the modern state of about 6,686 km2 (infobox). Cliopatria's row ends in 1894.

region.text: the Minangkabau chiefdoms of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Rembau, Johol and Jelai under the Yamtuan

ledger.note: 1773: the Sultan of Johor confirms Raja Melewar as Yamtuan Seri Menanti over the Minangkabau chiefdoms. The page dates the title to 1773 and the 'original nine chiefdoms' to 'the first incarnation of Negeri Sembilan in 1773'; the Minangkabau had come 'in the 15th century' and sought protection as Johor weakened and the Bugis attacked.

region.text: Naning, the chiefdom incorporated into the district of Malacca

ledger.note: 1832: Naning, one of the original nine chiefdoms, is incorporated into British Malacca. 'Naning was incorporated into the Straits Settlement of Malacca in 1832 following the Naning War.' The Naning War page: war from 6 August 1831, the British occupied Taboh on 15 June 1832, and 'Naning incorporated into the district of Malacca'; the Sultan of Johor had ceded his suzerainty over Naning to the Dutch in 1757, so the loss is of a nominal luak.

region.text: Sungai Ujong, the luak whose name Seremban once bore

ledger.note: 1874: the British intervene in Sungai Ujong and set up a Resident. 'In 1874, the British intervened militarily in a leadership tussle in Sungai Ujong'; the domain stays a separate Malay state under a British Resident until 1895 (the Battle of Paroi was fought in 1875, Gurkha reinforcements arrived on 10 December 1875). The Federated Malay States page agrees: the residency system 'was extended the same year to Selangor and Negeri Sembilan'. Cliopatria's shape drops Sungai Ujong a year early, in 1873.

1883: a British Resident is installed in Jelebu ('Jelebu followed in 1883'); Jelebu stays outside the Seri Menanti Confederation until 1895. Rembau followed in 1887, but it joined the 1889 confederation and is not lost here. Cliopatria keeps Jelebu in its shape to 1889.

1889: Seri Menanti, Tampin and Rembau form the Seri Menanti Confederation. 'The formation of modern Negeri Sembilan began in 1889, when the Seri Menanti domain' joined with Tampin and Rembau; Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined only in 1895.

region.text: Sungai Ujong, the luak whose name Seremban once bore

ledger.note: 1895: Sungai Ujong joins the confederation, forming the modern Negeri Sembilan. 'The domains of Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined this confederation in 1895.'
1895: Jelebu joins the confederation. 'The domains of Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined this confederation in 1895.'

1895: Negeri Sembilan joins the Federated Malay States under its first British Resident, Martin Lister (the page has Lister becoming the first British Resident and the state joining the Federated Malay States the same year); the Treaty of Federation 1895 took effect on 1 July 1896 (Federated Malay States page).

wars.name: Naning War
wars.outcome: British victory: the British reached Taboh on 15 June 1832 and incorporated Naning into the district of Malacca; Rembau's chiefs, met on 20 January 1832, supported the British and Rembau was later recognised as an independent state.
wars.note: Dates 6 August 1831 to 15 June 1832; Dol Said surrendered on 4 February 1834. Negeri Sembilan as a whole was not a belligerent; only Rembau, one luak, sided with the British.

wars.name: British intervention in Sungai Ujong

zones.text: Sungai Ujong, the luak whose name Seremban once bore

wars.outcome: The British backed one claimant in a leadership dispute, placed Sungai Ujong under a Resident (1874) and fought at Paroi in 1875; Yamtuan Antah's palace at Seri Menanti was destroyed during the Bukit Putus fighting.
wars.note: 'In 1875, British forces, accompanied by Arab mercenaries and Gurkha, engaged Malay defenders in Paroi'; reinforcements arrived 10 December 1875. The page does not date the end of the fighting, so no contest_end is recorded.

certainty.note: No page gives the extent of the nine luaks; the Cliopatria outline is approximate.
The British Residents' domains (Sungai Ujong 1874, Jelebu 1883, Rembau 1887) are named on the page without boundaries.

sources.title: Negeri Sembilan
sources.note: Infobox area 6,686 km2; 1773 nine chiefdoms and the Yamtuan Seri Menanti; Naning 1832; British Sungai Ujong 1874, Paroi 1875, Jelebu 1883, Rembau 1887; confederation 1889; union and FMS 1895; occupation 1942-1945.

sources.title: Sungai Ujong
sources.note: Thin: treats Sungai Ujong mainly as the old name of Seremban and gives no date for the British intervention, the Resident or the 1895 union.

sources.title: Naning War
sources.note: 6 August 1831 to 15 June 1832; Naning one of the nine luaks; Johor ceded its suzerainty to the Dutch in 1757; Rembau's support; incorporation into Malacca.

sources.title: Federated Malay States
sources.note: Residency system extended to Negeri Sembilan in 1874; Treaty of Federation 1895, in force 1 July 1896.

notes: Budget up to 5 pages: four used. Cliopatria's 1873, 1877 and 1890 changes read as Sungai Ujong leaving (page: British intervention 1874), a no-op in 1877, and the Seri Menanti Confederation of 1889 without Sungai Ujong and Jelebu; the outline is 'ok' for those readings. Not settled: the extents of the nine luaks (Klang, Segamat, Ulu Pahang and Naning left 'in the 19th century' with no year except Naning 1832); whether Cliopatria's outline holds Naning at all; why 1873 and not 1874; the date of the end of the Sungai Ujong fighting; when Seri Menanti became the capital (no date). The state does not end in 1895 in any real sense: it is the same Negeri Sembilan, a protected state of the FMS and later Malaya; the dissolve event only marks the end of its separate sovereignty, and the matching vassal/protectorate tint belongs to the federated-malay-states dossier (Cliopatria has no row for the FMS: the brief assigns it to the additions batch se-03-x). The Sungai Ujong page was nearly empty. Region names missing from the gazetteer: Naning (used as a region), Sungai Ujong, Jelebu and Rembau (the last two are drawn with a radius or a place name that exists).
